title: Crunchyroll’s Hottest New Shonen Anime Has Created the Perfect New Action Hero in Just Eight Episodes
content:
The Summer 2026 season is packed with diverse anime; however, it wouldn’t feel complete without a shonen anime, and this is exactly what Crunchyroll is providing with Black Torch . Since the start of the season, Black Torch has emerged as the perfect shonen anime, embracing familiar tropes that have defined the genre. One of the best elements Black Torch has incorporated is its main hero, who consistently embodies the qualities of a classic shonen protagonist. Jiro Azuma instantly emerges as the physically powerful and hopeful protagonist that a shonen hero usually represents.

However, what further amplified his position was the first episode giving him an inner demon power, a trope that has become synonymous with shonen protagonists. Jiro gains Rago, a legendary mononoke, the spirits that humans are currently at war with. The first episode itself solidified their bond, as Rago had to use Jiro as his vessel to heal from a fatal injury. Their bond has only progressed since then, with the seventh episode already seeing Jiro gain a new transformation that represents the pinnacle of their power. Now, the eighth episode of the series, the latest, has incorporated one more defining characteristic of a shonen protagonist, cementing Jiro as a perfect new action shonen hero.

Black Torch ‘s Protagonist Has Emerged as the Perfect New Action Shonen Hero

With all these elements established by the eighth episode, Jiro had already emerged as the perfect new shonen protagonist , possessing all the best traits of the genre. However, the latest episode also incorporated one more defining trait of a shonen hero that is usually only seen in the later stages of a series. After the latest major fight, Jiro and Rago are confronted by Amagi, the spirit leading the Mononoke in the current war. With Jiro unconscious after his latest transformation, Amagi forces Rago to join the Mononoke’s side, but Rago refuses. Fortunately, Jiro is saved by the arrival of the new team members, although Amagi still manages to capture Rago.

However, the twist at the end of the episode reveals that Rago gave all of his powers to Jiro, and now he is nothing more than a cat. This action from Rago has effectively eliminated the threat of Jiro gradually dying due to Rago consuming his vital energy, but the two have been separated, and Amagi seemingly also killed Rago. Jiro has already emerged as the shonen protagonist who has gained the perfect power but lost his companion. Fans have seen this trope with other shonen protagonists as well, with Naruto being the prime example, as he gained Baryon Mode through Kurama’s sacrifice.

These moments in a shonen hero’s journey often make it clear that their journey has reached its conclusion. However, Black Torch has already incorporated this trope, largely because the narrative of the series itself is very short. Adapting all 19 chapters of the manga is a quick job, and given the pacing, the series might actually conclude within three or four more episodes. Even with its short narrative, Black Torch has positioned its protagonist with the perfect shonen hero tropes, which only highlights that, had the original manga had a longer run , Black Torch might have emerged as an even better new shonen anime on Crunchyroll in 2026, becoming one of its mainstays alongside Jujutsu Kaisen , Demon Slayer , and Black Clover .

title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Game's Trailer Announces English Voice Cast
content:
Konami revealed the English voice cast for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, a new game in its Castlevania series, in a trailer on Monday.

• Abby Trott as Rose Belmont

• J.B. Blanc as Trevor Belmont

• Alejandra Reynoso as Sypha Belnades (reprising role from Castlevania animated series)

• Graham McTavish as Dracula (reprising role from Castlevania animated series)

• Ray Chase as The Fallen

• Erica Lindbeck as Joan of Arc

• Melique Berger as Medusa

• Liam O'Brien as Isaac (reprising role from Castlevania: Curse of Darkness game)

• Dawn M. Bennett as Carmilla

• Aaron LaPlante as Death

The game will launch on October 15 for the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox Cloud, Xbox PC, Nintendo Switch, and PC via Steam .

Konami describes the game:

Over two decades after the events of Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse and the recent animated show, it is in the streets of 15th century Paris that a new chapter of the legendary House Belmont is about to be written in bloody red ink. Armed with a legendary holy whip, the Vampire Killer, Trevor Belmont's successor – and the game's protagonist – must descend into the city attacked by monstrous creatures and a looming mystical castle to hunt down the beasts and save the Parisians from eternal darkness. Long-time fans and newcomers to the franchise will have to master different weapons and spells to arm themselves against foes. Plus, a sense of exploration will favor the bold and those who dare explore every inch of the sinister castle.

The game is the first entirely new game in the Castlevania franchise since Castlevania: Lords of Shadow 2 in 2014.

Konami released the Castlevania Dominus Collection on Switch, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam in August 2024. The collection includes the series' three Nintendo DS games Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow , Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin , and Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia . It also includes the first original Castlevania arcade game Haunted Castle and a reimagining titled Haunted Castle Revisited .

Castlevania: Nocturne , the spinoff series of Frederator Studios ' Castlevania animated show , premiered in September 2023. The series stars Richter Belmont (a descendant of the original show's protagonists Sypha and Trevor) and Maria Renard. The series is set in France during the French Revolution in 1792, and it is an origin story for Richter. The second season premiered in January 2025.

title: One Piece’s Most Powerful Elbaph Characters Get New Looks From Legendary Creator
content:
The Elbaph Arc in One Piece is by far the most intense and crucial phase of the story almost three decades after its debut. The story has long since entered its Final Saga, which is all the more reason that the Straw Hat Pirates are closer to Laughtale than ever. Not to mention that the mystery behind Void Century is finally starting to make sense with the pieces of the puzzle being put together. While fans await more secrets to be revealed, the Elbaph Arc introduced two unbelievably powerful characters. Loki, the Prince of Elbaph, was already mentioned in the Whole Cake Island Arc, but no one expected him to be the most powerful Giant alive.

Not only that, but the ongoing arc also confirmed the Shanks’ twin theory by introducing Shamrock Figarland, the Commander of the Holy Knights. As the two characters continue to gain massive popularity, Yoshitaka Amano drew their visuals for One Piece Card Game. Amano is a legendary artist and character designer best known for Vampire Hunter D, Angel’s Egg , and more. The gorgeous illustrations were shared by the official X handle of the series , which also confirmed that both characters are included in Booster Pack Volume 18, which will be released in November this year.

One Piece Has Yet to Reveal The True Extent of Loki and Shamrock’s Powers

While the series has only shown a glimpse of their powers, it’s more than enough to convince fans that they’re on a completely different level. Loki has the blood of the Ancient Giant running through his veins, so he was already powerful enough, but thanks to the legendary Devil Fruit, he can take on the form of a dragon to engulf the entire sky with his sky.

On the other hand, Shamrock is one of the major antagonists of the Elbaph Arc and the overarching plot. Despite being Shanks’ brother, he grew up in a completely different environment and became a ruthless Holy Knight. He left the Elbaph island not long after his introduction but demonstrated a fraction of his terrifying powers thanks to his sword, which can use the powers of a Mythical Zoan-Type Fruit.

One Piece ‘s Elbaph Arc Is Currently At a Crucial Phase

The Elbaph Arc began in September 2024 with Chapter 1126, and it wouldn’t be a surprise if the arc reached its conclusion in a few months. Instead of focusing primarily on fights, the arc focused on backstories and ancient lore. Thanks to the Harley text and the gigantic ancient mural, fans also know about the three worlds in the legends that are somehow tied to the Sun God Nika.

Following the backstory’s conclusion, the manga took an even more unexpected turn when Saint Nerona Imu arrived on the island . Imu is by far the most powerful opponent Luffy has ever faced, and he is nowhere near powerful enough to stop the villain. The situation in Elbaph went from bad to worse after Imu’s arrival, and things will only return to normal when the villain leaves the island.

title: One Piece May Have Just Lost Its Chance to Fix Its Biggest Fan Complaint
content:
One Piece manga is seeing things get very exciting in the Elbaph arc as the series’ supposed final villain, Imu, the King of the World, continues his dominance in the fight, which has also presented an opportunity to incorporate one of the series’ most missing elements that is becoming necessary now. However, the latest chapter might have lost that chance. In over two and a half decades of One Piece ‘s serialization, the series has incorporated almost every element known for making a story compelling. This is solidified by how the series has introduced hundreds of characters that add to its diversity.

However, there is still one element that the series has largely refrained from, and it is death. To be precise, One Piece does feature deaths, but they almost always occur in backstories, something fans have become accustomed to given the context, while the series rarely features major deaths in real time. The last major deaths that added an element of surprise to the series came during the Marineford arc, with Ace’s death and Whitebeard also dying at the end of the arc. Since then, there has been no major death in real time, and the series even brought back Saul, who was supposedly dead. Amid this, however, the Elbaph arc had created an opportunity to feature this element, with Scopper Gaban being positioned for it, but the series has now seemingly squandered that opportunity.

One Piece Misses the Chance to Feature an Emotional Death in the Elbaph Arc

Scopper Gaban has been one of the more mysterious characters of the Elbaph arc, but he has constantly become a lovable character through his nuances, while also emerging as a new teacher to Luffy and the Straw Hats, giving his character even more gravity. As Luffy and Imu’s battle escalated, with Imu proving the difference in their strength, Gaban intervened and saved Luffy from death. With Luffy down and Gaban insisting that there is still more for him to learn , Gaban took on Imu alone and positioned himself as a sacrifice, as evident from how Imu was able to cut off one of his hands.

Given that Gaban had an emotional impact on Luffy, his death in the latest chapter would have provided the emotional growth Luffy needed. However, the latest chapter sees Hajrudin, Loki, and even Luffy get back up to fight Imu, effectively removing the position in which Gaban could have died. This not only loses the opportunity to feature a compelling death but also undermines Imu’s presence as a strong and evil final villain. The death of a compelling character at Imu’s hands would have solidified his position as the ruthless King of the World who has ruled for centuries.

But the series is losing this opportunity as the new chapter highlights that the strength of the union is still greater than that of the King of the World, even amid the chaos, where the Straw Hats still have to learn new techniques to fight these immortal villains. If the series follows through with this, One Piece might still give Luffy the emotional growth he needs while once again highlighting the need for training and the sacrifices he still has to make to become the Pirate King. But for now, One Piece yet again refrains from employing character deaths, despite having hundreds of characters and the opportunity to fix one of the biggest complaints fans have about the series.

title: Marvelous Teases New Story of Seasons, Rune Factory 6 Games
content:
Marvelous teased its next title in the Story of Seasons game franchise with footage on Monday, along with the first footage of Rune Factory 6 during the "Story of Seasons 30th Anniversary and Rune Factory 20th Anniversary" livestream.

Story of Seasons Teaser

Rune Factory 6 Teaser

The Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar remake game launched for Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam in August 2025. The game launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on May 28. The game originally launched for the Nintendo DS in Japan in 2008. Natsume released it in English under the title Harvest Moon DS: Grand Bazaar in 2010.

The game was one of two new Story of Seasons games that Marvelous is planning, with one being a single player game, and the other being a multiplayer game.

Marvelous had announced in 2023 that is developing both Rune Factory 6 as a new game in its RPG/farming game franchise.

The Rune Factory: Guardians of Azuma ( Ryū no Kuni Rune Factory ) game launched worldwide for Switch and PC via Steam in May 2025. The game got a Switch 2 version in June 2025 at the console's launch and PS5 and Xbox X|S releases on February 13. The game was formerly known as Rune Factory: Project Dragon .

title: RetroCrush Adds Guyver OVA, Live-Action Dororo Film
content:
RetroCrush announced on August 1 it will add the live-action Dororo film with Japanese audio and the English dubbed version of The Guyver: Bio-Booster Armor , the OVA adaptation of Yoshiki Takaya 's Bio-Booster Armor Guyver manga , on August 21. Both titles are available to stream now.

The streamer is also adding the following titles through the month of August:

• Lone Wolf and Cub (TV series) - now available

• Gonjam: Haunted Asylum - now available

• Shogun's Mission - now available

• Bounty Hunter season 1 - now available

• Lethal Three: Sanbiki ga Kiru! - August 28

Takaya's Bio-Booster Armor Guyver manga inspired an OVA series from 1989-1992, a television anime from 2005-2006, and two live-action films. Viz Media released part of the manga in English from 1995-1998, Manga Entertainment released the OVAs in North America, and ADV Films and later FUNimation Entertainment released the television anime.

Vertical previously released Osamu Tezuka 's original 1967 Dororo manga in three volumes, and in a collected omnbius volume in 2012.

The supernatural historical manga previously inspired a 26-episode black-and-white anime series in 1969 by Tezuka Productions . A new television anime premiered in January 2019. Sentai Filmworks licensed the anime.

Satoshi Shiki launched a Dororo remake manga titled The Legend of Dororo and Hyakkimaru ( Dororo to Hyakkimaru -den ) in Akita Shoten 's Monthly Champion RED magazine in October 2018. The series ended in the 13th volume on December 19. Seven Seas Entertainment is releasing the manga.

Japanese distributor Media Do , Tezuka Production, and South Korean comic company Copin Communications launched a Japanese-South Korean vertical-scrolling webcomic remake of Osamu Tezuka 's classic Dororo manga titled Dororo Re:Verse in 2022.

title: Bleach Might Retcon Its Finale’s Most Divisive Scene With Time Travel Twist
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War made a massive change to the anime’s final arc with the latest episode of the series, and it might be on the verge of fixing a major issue that fans had with the original manga with a new time travel twist. Bleach ended its original manga run ten long years ago, and the final season of its new era of the anime has been making all sorts of adjustments thanks to creator Tite Kubo’s close work with the anime team. But the latest change happens to be the biggest yet.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War just made a huge change to the anime that not only saw Ichigo reveal a brand new Bankai form never seen in the original events of the manga, but it also seemingly led to the death of Orihime Inoue. But while this is a massive change to the series’ canon, it’s also surprisingly a way that the franchise can retcon the fact that Ichigo never got to use this new Bankai in the original. It’s sparked a whole new timeline, and it could return to the main timeline with a twist in a future episode.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Just Revealed A Whole New Timeline

In Bleach’ s original manga, at this point in the final fight against Yhwach, he had used his Almighty power to break Ichigo’s Zanpakuto before he could enact his Bankai. Shortly after he had claimed that he saw into the future, and thus broke the Bankai as a sign of some twisted form of respect for Ichigo’s power. Almighty was then explained to not be a power that simply lets him see into the future, but instead allows him to alter the future across the many potential timelines that Yhwach is seeing at all times.

So while this is a huge change from how the manga played out, it fits perfectly into the events of the final arc of the series. Ichigo was able to unleash his new Bankai, and Orihime seemingly unleashed her true power to defeat Yhwach once and for all. This is likely just a whole new timeline that fans are getting to see play out in the anime, and could then all be wrapped back into the official “canon” events of the series once Yhwach uses his Almighty to then return to the series’ manga adaptation.

What Does This Mean for Bleach’s Anime Future?

With Orihime seemingly dying at the end of the latest episode, Yhwach resetting this timeline would be the ultimate official retcon in all senses of the word. This huge change to the anime has resulted in the most successful episode with fans to date , and it’s no surprise as to why given that the franchise might be using this as a way to further expand on that final battle with Yhwach. Fans have been complaining for a very long time that it had been rushed, and that was because it actually was being pushed along by Shueisha at the time.

Bleach at the time of its ending was doing not well with Shonen Jump as it was selling worse than other emerging hits at the time, and it’s why the anime even got cancelled long before it even approached an adaptation of the final arc. This led to a truncated version of the final battle between Ichigo and Yhwach, and now Kubo gets to use this episode as a way to showcase what Almighty truly is while giving Orihime a big moment at the same time. But it all depends on whether or not the anime continues to change even more as it heads to the grand finale.

Bleach ended its original manga run ten long years ago, and the final season of its new era of the anime has been making all sorts of adjustments thanks to creator Tite Kubo’s close work with the anime team. But the latest change happens to be the biggest yet.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War just made a huge change to the anime that not only saw Ichigo reveal a brand new Bankai form never seen in the original events of the manga, but it also seemingly led to the death of Orihime Inoue. But while this is a massive change to the series’ canon, it’s also surprisingly a way that the franchise can retcon the fact that Ichigo never got to use this new Bankai in the original. It’s sparked a whole new timeline, and it could return to the main timeline with a twist in a future episode.
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Just Revealed A Whole New Timeline

In Bleach’ s original manga, at this point in the final fight against Yhwach, he had used his Almighty power to break Ichigo’s Zanpakuto before he could enact his Bankai. Shortly after he had claimed that he saw into the future, and thus broke the Bankai as a sign of some twisted form of respect for Ichigo’s power. Almighty was then explained to not be a power that simply lets him see into the future, but instead allows him to alter the future across the many potential timelines that Yhwach is seeing at all times.

So while this is a huge change from how the manga played out, it fits perfectly into the events of the final arc of the series. Ichigo was able to unleash his new Bankai, and Orihime seemingly unleashed her true power to defeat Yhwach once and for all. This is likely just a whole new timeline that fans are getting to see play out in the anime, and could then all be wrapped back into the official “canon” events of the series once Yhwach uses his Almighty to then return to the series’ manga adaptation.
What Does This Mean for Bleach’s Anime Future?

With Orihime seemingly dying at the end of the latest episode, Yhwach resetting this timeline would be the ultimate official retcon in all senses of the word. This huge change to the anime has resulted in the most successful episode with fans to date , and it’s no surprise as to why given that the franchise might be using this as a way to further expand on that final battle with Yhwach. Fans have been complaining for a very long time that it had been rushed, and that was because it actually was being pushed along by Shueisha at the time.

Bleach at the time of its ending was doing not well with Shonen Jump as it was selling worse than other emerging hits at the time, and it’s why the anime even got cancelled long before it even approached an adaptation of the final arc. This led to a truncated version of the final battle between Ichigo and Yhwach, and now Kubo gets to use this episode as a way to showcase what Almighty truly is while giving Orihime a big moment at the same time. But it all depends on whether or not the anime continues to change even more as it heads to the grand finale.

title: K Manga Adds Daiki Yamazaki's Golden Phantom Manga
content:
The company describes the series:

While on an outing to an amusement park with his family to celebrate his daughter's middle school graduation, Shingo Asahina encounters a mysterious man covered in blood being pursued by some unsavory characters. On the spur of the moment, he gets on the Ferris wheel with the wounded man to shelter him. When questioned, the man simply says “In 30 minutes, this amusement park will turn into hell on Earth,” and explains that in order to prevent disaster, he needs to “borrow” Shingo's body…

Yamazaki ( Chaos Game ) debuted the manga in Kodansha 's Afternoon magazine on February 25. The first compiled book volume shipped in Japan on July 22.

Yamazaki launched the Chaos Game manga in Kodansha 's Afternoon magazine in July 2022, and ended it in June 2024. Kodansha published the manga's fifth and final compiled book volume in September 2024. Kodansha 's K MANGA service published Chaos Game in English.

Yamazaki published the "Kishibe no Yume" one-shot manga in Kodansha 's Moae magazine in 2022.

title: Netflix Confirms Release Date for New Horror Anime From Legendary Studios & Fans Aren’t Happy
content:
Netflix has confirmed the release date and schedule for a new horror thriller anime hitting later this year, but unfortunately fans are not happy with the streaming service right now. Netflix took the stage during the Anime NYC 2026 weekend to give fans a major update about all of the new projects they now have in the works, and that includes some big licenses that fans have been wanting to see. But unfortunately for some of these highly anticipated releases, the Netflix binge release model won’t exactly be a great fit.

Kasumi Yasuda’s Fool Night is gearing up to make its official anime adaptation debut with Netflix later this November, and has dropped a full new look showing off what to expect from its highly anticipated premiere. But unfortunately it has also confirmed that all of its episodes will be releasing at once rather than dropping weekly. And fans are not happy that the series’ mystery won’t get a chance to flesh out in the way they were hoping for. Check out the new trailer and special interview video for Fool Night below.

When Does Fool Night Come Out on Netflix?

Fool Night will be making its worldwide debut with Netflix on November 26th, and will be releasing all of its episodes at once. It’s going to be a joint production between two legendary anime studios with Atsuyuki Yukawa directing the anime for Sunrise ( Mobile Suit Gundam ) and Shaft ( Puella Magi Madoka Magica ), Jin Tanaka handling the series composition, Robert Sato providing the character designs, and Tatsuya Kato composing the music. So it’s going to both look and sound great.

The main voice cast of Fool Night has been confirmed as well with Koki Uchiyama as Toshiro Kamiya, Minako Kotobuki as Yomiko Horai, Junya Enoki as Akira Yatsuka, Aya Endo as Saeko Kanaeno, and Kiyomitsu Mizuuchi as Jin Hiragishi. Netflix has confirmed that the series will also be launching with an English dub, and it will be led by Adam McArthur as Toshiro and Olivia Liang as Yomiko. Thankfully it won’t be too much longer before fans get to see this new series in action.

What Is Fool Night?

Kasumi Yasuda’s Fool Night manga has been a standout with Shogakukan’s Big Comic Superior magazine ever since it made its debut back in 2020, and it’s no mystery as to why as the franchise sparks a cool new mystery in a dark world. With oxygen running out, humanity has resorted to planting flowers and other plants within dying people in a process known as “Transfloration” that keeps that minimal oxygen supply going for as long as it can. But it seems like it’s all going to hit right at once.

Netflix’s release strategy has been changing quite a lot with its anime premieres in the last few years, and it’s meant that a lot of the newer hits have been able to drop their new episodes on a weekly basis much like their initial debuts in Japan. This is a far cry from the binge releases that used to come months after the fact that the streaming service used to do, but when it occasionally happens it still comes as a bummer for those fans hoping to see the series getting to flesh out over several weeks and spark discussion that way. It’s still possible, but fans are going to need to work that much harder.

title: Japanese Animation TV Ranking, August 10-16
content:
The Kodoku no Gourmet Special! Manatsu no Tohoku・Miyagi Shucchō-hen ( Solitary Gourmet Special! Midsummer Business Trip to Tohoku and Miyagi) live-action special aired on TV Tokyo on Tuesday, August 11 at 5:50 p.m. and it earned a 5.7% rating.

The Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind anime film aired on NTV on Friday, August 14 at 9:00 p.m. and earned an 8.3% rating.

The Night on the Galactic Railroad anime film aired on NHK-E on Tuesday, August 11 at 9:00 a.m. and it earned a 0.8% rating.

The television ratings above are an estimate of the percentage of the population that watch a given program, based on data from a survey of households in Japan's Kanto region. The ratings do not count recordings that viewers watch later.
